verdict.rationale: n8n documents a first-party MCP Server Trigger node (n8n-docs-19, n8n-probe-3), which lets a workflow act as an MCP server that external agents can call. Combined with its 1500+ integrations (n8n-gh-2), this covers the core of exposing workflows and connected app actions as MCP tools. The evidence is only a docs title and a probe pointer, though. Missing for 10: details on how workflows and app actions are mapped to MCP tools, transport/auth specifics, and independent or hands-on corroboration of external agents calling n8n MCP tools.
